v: Therefore I take pleasure in weaknesses, in injuries, in necessities, in persecutions, and in distresses, for Christ’s sake. For when I am weak, then am I strong.
b: This verse tells us that a Christian's joy is not like what the world thinks, which exists only when things are smooth and comfortable; because of Christ we can find joy even in hardship. For Christ's sake, the weaknesses, insults, necessities, persecutions, and distresses we face all become our joy. For through these sufferings we come to know Christ more and gain Christ, and Christ is the greatest treasure of our lives.

An athlete was preparing for an important competition. He had gone through countless training sessions and difficulties, and had also met setbacks and failures. But he did not lose heart because of them; instead he drew strength and motivation from them. Every failure and difficulty made him pursue success more firmly. In the end he won the competition and became an outstanding athlete.

This story tells us that in life we too will meet all kinds of challenges and hardships, but we must not be defeated by them. Instead, we should face these difficulties with a joyful spirit, because they will make us stronger and more mature. As the apostle Paul said, when we are weak, then we can be strong in the power of Christ.

Let us face the difficulties and adversities of life every day with a joyful spirit. Do not let them defeat us, but overcome them through the power of Christ. Let us remember that God shows His great power in our weakness, and that He will be with us and lead us through difficulties.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you find joy and strength in every difficulty, and face life courageously with the power of Christ. Amen!

v: Is any among you suffering? Let him pray. Is any cheerful? Let him sing praises.
b: In this verse God calls us, whether in suffering or in joy, to respond to Him with prayer and praise. Let us think: when we meet suffering, how can we find strength and comfort through prayer?

There was an old grandmother, aged and living alone, whose life was lonely and hard. Every day she faced all kinds of difficulties, but she never gave up hope and faith. She understood that prayer is the way to connect with God, so she handed all her worries and pressures over to God and entrusted them to Him. Every night she prepared a small corner especially for talking with God. Her prayer was not only her personal conversation, but also her way of finding strength and wisdom in difficulty. She believed that prayer is a power that can change life, and she experienced many miracles and wonders.

At the same time, we must also understand that in joy, praise is a must. When we have gladness, we should open our hearts and sing to God with mouths of thanksgiving and praise. Take a young man who, after graduating from university, found an ideal job and achieved success in his career. Yet he did not forget everything God had given him; he deeply understood that these achievements were not only his own effort, but God's blessing. Every morning he would stop to thank God, and face each day with a heart of delight and gratitude. His joy affected not only himself but also infected those around him, and he became a witness to the pursuit of joy.

Dear family, when we pray in suffering, we can find God's strength and comfort. When we praise in joy, we can share God's blessing and joy. So whatever situation we are in, let us respond to God's love and grace with prayer and praise.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you find strength and comfort in suffering, and feel God's blessing and joy in gladness. Amen!

v: looking to Jesus, the author and perfecter of faith, who for the joy that was set before him endured the cross, despising its shame, and has sat down at the right hand of the throne of God.
b: In life we often meet all kinds of challenges and difficulties. We often feel tired and helpless, as if we cannot find the motivation to go forward. But when we look to Jesus, who is the author and perfecter of our faith, He will lead us through difficulties and bring us to the shore of victory. It is like a person climbing a high mountain. The whole way is full of rugged paths and obstacles, and he feels very weary and confused. But he lifts his head and looks at the beautiful view at the top, and sees a broad plain and lovely scenery waiting for him. This view becomes his motivation for the climb, enabling him to overcome the difficulties and keep going to the summit. In the same way, when we look to Jesus and see Him seated at the right hand of the throne of God, we too can gain strength and hope from it.

Jesus set an excellent example for our faith. Because of the joy of glorious resurrection set before Him, He endured the shame and suffering of the cross, and in the end won the victory. This reminds us that the difficulties we face are only temporary, while the joy ahead is eternal. Just as Jesus despised the suffering before Him for the joy set before Him, when we face challenges with love, hope, and perseverance, we too can rise above present difficulties and welcome the joy to come.

Let us look to Jesus together and, like Him, walk through hardship without wavering and overcome difficulties. Believe that as long as we put our faith in Him, He will surely lead us to the destination of the joy that is set before us.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you look to Jesus without wavering when you face difficulties, believing that He will surely lead you out of trouble and into the joy ahead. Amen!

v: You have turned my mourning into dancing for me. You have removed my sackcloth, and clothed me with gladness,
b: In our lives we inevitably meet hardship and challenge, and we may feel sorrow, loss, or discouragement. But God's word reminds us that He can turn our mourning into dancing and exchange our sorrow for joy.

In a small village lived a girl named Xiaomei. Her life was not easy; she bore the responsibility of caring for her aged parents and young brothers and sisters, and life was hard. But she never gave up, and always kept a smile and firm faith.

One day the village held a dance, and everyone looked forward to it, because it was their chance to escape reality and enjoy a night of gladness. But Xiaomei felt discouraged by the pressures of life, and did not know how to face the dance.

Just as she was about to give up, an old man came up to her and asked why she was not happy. Xiaomei told him about her difficulties and pressures. After listening, the old man said to Xiaomei, “Do you know? God can turn your mourning into dancing. At this dance, you can move your feet, lay down all your burdens, and let God's joy fill your heart.”

Hearing this, Xiaomei was surprised and encouraged, and she decided to believe God's word. At the dance, Xiaomei danced to the music like a beautiful flower in full bloom. She forgot all her sorrows and worries, and her heart was filled with joy and peace.

This story tells us that even when we are in difficulty, God can change our situation and turn sorrow into joy. As the Psalm says, God will turn our mourning into dancing, remove our sackcloth, and clothe us with gladness.
So whatever difficulties and challenges we face, let us look for strength and hope in God's word. Believe that He can change our circumstances and bring us joy and peace.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you be clothed with God's joy in all your difficulties. Amen!

v: rejoicing in hope, enduring in troubles, continuing steadfastly in prayer,
b: We live in a world full of challenges and difficulties, and everyone may meet all kinds of trouble and disappointment. Sometimes we may feel discouraged and let down, not knowing how to go on.

Yet this verse reminds us that in the face of difficulty we can find joy in hope. The hope here does not mean longing for the future, but our faith in and dependence on God. When we believe in God's existence and His love for us, we can find the source of joy deep within.

It is like a farmer who worked hard on his land in a dry summer and sowed many seeds. But after several months of wind and sun, the field turned yellow and withered, and the seeds did not sprout. The farmer looked at all this and felt very discouraged and disappointed. But he did not give up; he still kept his hope for a future harvest and kept working to care for the field.
In the end, when autumn came, the rain finally fell, and the farmer's field turned green and full of life again. His hope and effort were finally rewarded, and the harvest exceeded his expectations.

In life we too often need to be like the farmer, keeping hope for a good future in the midst of difficulty. Although our present situation may be hard, as long as we believe in God's love and His plan, we can face challenges calmly and rejoice for the good to come.

In addition, this verse also reminds us to endure in troubles. The sufferings and pains of life sometimes make us lose heart and feel we cannot go on. Yet this is exactly when we need to persevere. Just as athletes face all kinds of difficulties in training, but can win only by keeping on, we also need to endure in difficulty, believing that God will surely lead us through.

Finally, prayer is our way of communicating with God, and it is also the source on which we can keep relying on Him. When we face difficulties, we can pray continually, asking God for strength, wisdom, and courage. Prayer lets us build a deeper connection with God, and lets us hand all our worries and burdens over to God, so that through the Lord who loves us we may be more than conquerors in all things,
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you rejoice in hope and hold on in endurance in troubles. May your prayer be steadfast, and may you experience God's great power overcoming all troubles. Amen!

v: Rejoice with those who rejoice. Weep with those who weep.
b: In this busy world we often face all kinds of challenges and difficulties. Sometimes we feel happy and glad, but at other times we feel sad and sorrowful. Yet God's word reminds us that in all this we need to rejoice together and weep together.

When we are in joy, we should share this joy with those who rejoice. This is not only for mutual inspiration and encouragement, but also so that the joy may spread, letting more people feel God's blessing and delight. Just as one candle can light countless candles, our joy can also infect others, bringing boundless gladness and blessing.

And when we are in sorrow and grief, we also need to weep together. There is so much suffering and pain in this world that we cannot avoid moments of sadness. But in this sorrow we can lean on and support one another, letting each other feel comfort and warmth. Just as an umbrella can give protection, our sympathy and care can also give others strength and hope.

A kind young man passed through a park one stormy night and saw a person crying alone in the rain. Moved with compassion, he went over and asked why the person was crying. The person told him he had lost a dearly loved family member. After listening, the young man said nothing; he only quietly took his hand and stood in the rain beside him. In that moment they felt each other's pain, and found a bit of comfort and strength in each other.

This story tells us that when we can rejoice and weep with others, we can build sincere connections and support one another in our difficulties. This is not only an exchange between people, but also an expression of God's love flowing among us. For only through shared joy and sorrow can we experience God's grace and promises more deeply.

Dear family, let us receive God's word together: rejoice with those who rejoice, and support those who grieve. Let us treat one another with love and care, so that whether in joy or in sorrow, we can find strength and comfort in each other.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you gain more love and wisdom as you share joy and sorrow with others. May you become sunshine in the lives of those around you, letting God's love flow out through your life. Amen!

v: Make us glad for as many days as you have afflicted us, for as many years as we have seen evil.
b: In life we all face all kinds of difficulties and challenges. Sometimes these difficulties may leave us feeling discouraged and without confidence. But this verse reminds us that God is with us in our difficulties and sufferings, and He wants to make us glad.

There was a girl named Catherine who lived in a poor family. Every day she had to do recycling work in exchange for a little food. Although life was very hard, Catherine always kept an optimistic attitude and a joyful heart.

One day Catherine met a rich and compassionate man, who saw Catherine's perseverance and joy and decided to help her. He gave her a gift full of food and clothing, and offered her a chance to receive an education and change her future.
This story tells us that even in difficult circumstances we can keep a joyful heart. The strength and hope God gives us are like that rich and compassionate man: they can change our lives.

Whatever difficulties we face, God is at our side. He wants to use these difficulties to shape our character and make us stronger. When we entrust our difficulties to Him, He will walk with us through every hard day.

So let us, like Catherine, keep a joyful heart, believe God's promises, and look forward to His work in our lives. When we bring joy into our lives, we will also infect those around us, letting them see God's love and grace.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you keep a joyful heart in difficulty and believe in God's great power. May His peace and joy fill your soul. Amen!

v: Rejoice in the Lord always! Again I will say, “Rejoice!”
b: In this passage Paul teaches us to rejoice always in the Lord Jesus. This world is full of pressure, difficulties, and challenges, but whatever we face, we can find joy in the Lord.
There was a man named David, who was a joyful and brave warrior. His life met with many difficulties and trials, but he was always able to find the spring of joy in hardship.

Once, David was pursued by his enemies and trapped in a cave. He felt despair and fear, but he turned to the Lord and asked for help. He began to sing psalms and praise, expressing his faith and joy. He believed that God would surely save him, and so his heart was filled with joy.

Like David, when we face difficulties, we can learn to seek joy from the Lord. This does not mean we have to hide our pain or deny our trouble, but to face them through faith, believing that God is at work in them.

There was a young man named Alex, who was disabled and could not walk. Every day he faced many difficulties and challenges, but he never gave up. He often sang hymns praising God, and found joy in hardship.
One day someone asked Alex, “How can you be so joyful? Your life is so hard!”
Alex answered, “Although I cannot walk, I can feel the Lord's love and grace. I know He is always with me, and this gives me endless joy and courage.”
This story tells us that whatever our situation, we can receive joy from the Lord. It is not only a feeling, but an inner strength that enables us to stand firm in difficulty.
So let us rejoice in the Lord always, every day. Whatever we face, let us seek God's face in hardship, believe His word, and discover the spring of joy.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you rejoice in the Lord always in all circumstances, for He is our true joy and hope. Amen!

v: But I rejoice in the Lord greatly that now at length you have revived your thought for me; in which you did indeed take thought, but you lacked opportunity.
b: In this passage the apostle Paul tells the believers of the church in Philippi that he felt boundless joy in the Lord Jesus Christ. Their concern and thoughts for him made him feel comforted and satisfied. Although they had always been thinking of him, for various reasons they had no chance to meet. Yet Paul's joy did not lessen; it only increased.

This passage reminds us of an important truth: joy does not depend on outward circumstances or conditions, but comes from our relationship with the Lord Jesus Christ. Paul experienced joy in difficulty and adversity because he deeply understood that God's love and grace never change. There was a little boy named Zhiguang who lived in a poor family. Although he faced all kinds of difficulties and challenges, Zhiguang always met each day with hope and joy. He knew he was not alone, because God's love and care were always with him. Though he might not have abundant food or expensive toys, his heart was full of gratitude and joy, because he knew he had God's love and a beautiful eternal home waiting for him.

This story reminds us that even in difficult circumstances we can have joy. When we place our hope and faith in the Lord Jesus Christ, we can experience the joy God gives us in any situation. Like Paul, we can rejoice steadfastly in adversity, because we know that God's love and grace endure.

So let us decide today to build a closer relationship with the Lord Jesus, and let His joy fill our hearts. Whatever difficulties or challenges we face, let us remember Paul's words and rejoice greatly in the Lord. For in the Lord we can find true joy and satisfaction.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you have a joyful heart every day, and find strength and hope in difficulty. Amen!

v: You will show me the path of life. In your presence is fullness of joy. In your right hand there are pleasures forever more.
b: This passage reminds us that as we walk the path of life, God guides us and leads us to true contentment and joy. It is a joy that goes beyond the world, a joy that comes from our relationship with God.

There was a man named Mingyang who felt empty and unsatisfied as he chased after money, career, and status. He felt he was always running after things yet never found real happiness or delight. Then one day he realized that the true value of life does not lie in pursuing material satisfaction, but in building an intimate relationship with God.

He began to read the Bible and pray, to talk with God, and to seek God’s will. As time went by, he found that when he was with God, his heart was filled with peace and joy. This joy did not come from outward success or pleasure, but from the way his relationship with God made him feel satisfied and glad.

Each of us can be like Mingyang and pursue this joy that goes beyond the world. By building an intimate relationship with God, we can let Him guide our path of life. When we focus on God’s will and entrust ourselves to Him, we will find fullness of joy in His presence and experience pleasures forever in His right hand.

Let us seek to draw closer to God every day and let Him guide our steps. Whatever difficulties or challenges we face, let us remember that in God’s presence there is fullness of joy, and in His right hand there are pleasures forever.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you find true joy and contentment in your relationship with God. Amen!

v: Satisfy us in the morning with your loving kindness, that we may rejoice and be glad all our days.
b: This passage comes from Psalm 90:14, and it reminds us how to experience joy and gladness in life. God’s lovingkindness is boundless. No matter what our circumstances, when we are satisfied in God’s lovingkindness, we can feel joy from deep within.

A young woman had met with many setbacks and hardships in life, yet she always kept her faith and hope in God. One day she was in a serious accident and her body was badly injured, but she was not defeated by it. Instead, she chose to use her experience to encourage and inspire others. She began sharing her story on social media and formed a support group with others, so that everyone could experience God’s lovingkindness and joy together. Though her life was not perfect, her life told us this: no matter how great the difficulties and challenges we face, if we trust in God, His lovingkindness will fill us with joy.

This sister’s story makes us wonder whether we, too, can hold on to our faith in adversity and find joy and gladness in it. Sometimes we may fall into trouble or feel discouraged, but when we remember God’s lovingkindness and faithfulness, we can see the beauty and joy in life. As the psalm says, when we are satisfied early with God’s lovingkindness, our hearts will be filled with joy and will rejoice.

Let us seek God’s lovingkindness every day, whether in ordinary life or in times of difficulty, and let us rejoice freely and feel the power of joy. For God’s lovingkindness is everlasting, and this joy will stay with us all our days.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you experience God’s lovingkindness and joy every day. Amen!

v: I have spoken these things to you, that my joy may remain in you, and that your joy may be made full.
b: In this passage, Jesus shares good news with His disciples: He wants to place His joy in their hearts and make their joy full. This is not only a promise but also a revelation, telling us where joy comes from and how to receive true joy in life.

There was a young man named Xinrong. Xinrong lived in a family with many problems and often felt helpless and disappointed. But he had a gift, and that was music. Every evening Xinrong sat by the window and played his violin, letting the music fill his soul.

One day Xinrong met a music teacher who recognized his talent and began to teach him more advanced techniques. As time passed, Xinrong’s music grew better and better, and he began to win top prizes in music competitions. This delight and sense of fulfillment brought true richness to Xinrong’s soul.

Do you know, each of us has gifts and unique qualities like Xinrong’s. When God created us, He gave each of us different talents and callings. When we discover and use these gifts, our hearts are filled with joy and satisfaction.

Yet true joy comes not only from our talents and achievements; it also comes from our relationship with God. When we build an intimate relationship with God and make Him the center of our lives, we receive true joy and satisfaction from Him.

In our daily lives we may meet difficulties and setbacks, but in those moments we can rely on God’s word and promises. When we store His words in our hearts, His joy becomes the driving force and source of energy for our lives.

So today, let us not only pursue the pleasures of the world, but seek the true joy that comes from God. Let us hide His word in our hearts and live out the calling and gifts He has given us. When we walk with God, His joy will fill our hearts and make our joy full.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you receive abundant joy on your journey of seeking joy. Amen!

v: The heart knows its own bitterness and joy; he will not share these with a stranger.
b: In life, everyone goes through all kinds of challenges and difficulties, and sometimes we feel helpless and bitter at heart. But this verse reminds us that only we ourselves know the state of our own hearts, and outsiders cannot fully understand. Yet in these words we can also find hope and courage.

Think of a person whose day is full of challenges and pain, facing pressure at work, problems at home, and health difficulties. Every day he walks down the street with a smile and greets people, but only he knows the pressure and pain inside. Yet he does not let these difficulties drag him down; he chooses to keep a positive and hopeful attitude.

Or think of a little blade of grass growing in the crack of a rock. The rock is scorched by the sun and has no source of water. Even so, the little grass keeps on growing and gives thanks each day to the sunlight and the earth. Whatever the outside difficulties, the little grass is never discouraged and uses its small strength to bring beauty to the world.

From these examples we can learn an important truth: even in bitterness we can still keep joy in our hearts. This is not pretending or denying reality; it is an expression of faith and hope. When we entrust our troubles to God and believe in His promises and love, we will find joy and peace in our hearts.

So whatever difficulty or pain you are going through, in this world only you can truly understand the state of your own heart. But please also remember that you are not alone; God is with you. Whatever you face, trust in His grace and strength, and let Him be the fountain of your joy.
pr: Dear Lord, thank You for being with us in our bitterness. Give us strength and joy, so that we can face difficulties with Your love. May our hearts be filled with Your peace and joy, and may we spread Your love in this world.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you feel God’s grace and love every day. Amen!

v: A glad heart makes a cheerful face, but an aching heart breaks the spirit.
b: This passage reminds us how important it is to have a joyful heart, because it not only brings happiness to ourselves but also influences others. When we have inner joy, smiles naturally show on our faces, and the people around us feel our gladness and warmth.

An elderly woman lived in a small village, and every day she planted beautiful flowers at her front door. These flowers brought joy to her and also brought lovely color and vitality to the whole village. Every day, people passing by were drawn to the beauty of the flowers, and their worries seemed to ease a little.

This woman’s joy and love were shown not only in planting flowers but also in her care and help for the people around her. She often gave others encouragement and help, and with her love she lit up the lives of many. A person so full of joy and love is not only a delight to her own soul but also good news to those around her.

In our own lives we can be like this woman, and through our manner, words, and actions let the light of joy and love shine out. When we are full of joy, we will actively care for others and give them encouragement and help. Such actions make others feel valued and loved, and they also enrich our own lives.

So let us seek the source of joy every day, whether in gatherings with family and friends or in fellowship with God. Let joy well up from our hearts and fill our faces with smiles, and let us share this joy with those around us.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. In your daily life, may you kindle the flame of joy and love and become a blessing to others. Amen!

v: The light of the eyes rejoices the heart. Good news gives health to the bones.
b: In life we often face all kinds of challenges and difficulties, and these problems may leave us feeling discouraged and disappointed. But this verse teaches us that when we see hope and positive things, our hearts are filled with joy.

A young girl named Yawen was an excellent student, but her family life was not happy. Her parents quarreled often, and this put great pressure on her. Yet Yawen did not give up. She chose to focus on the things that made her happy, such as reading, drawing, and helping others.

One day Yawen received good news. She had taken first place in her class on an exam, and her teacher praised her effort and talent. This good news filled Yawen’s heart with joy, and she felt as light as if she were flying in the sky.

This story tells us that even when there is darkness and difficulty in life, we can still find light and joy. Like Yawen, when we pay attention to and work toward the things that make us happy, our hearts will be filled with gladness, and this gladness will nourish our souls and give us courage to face any difficulty. A little sapling was growing in a forest. Although its surroundings were harsh, the sapling kept on growing. It never stopped absorbing sunlight, water, and nutrients, and it worked hard to stretch upward. In the end the little sapling grew into a tall tree and brought life and joy to the forest.

Like that sapling, we too must keep pursuing light and hope. When we turn our eyes to God and seek His will and truth, our souls will be filled with joy. Just as “the light of the eyes rejoices the heart,” we must let God’s love and truth enter our hearts so that our souls are filled with joy.

Good news is also a fountain that nourishes our lives. When we hear God’s word, or see God at work in our lives, our souls are also nourished. As Proverbs says, good news gives health to the bones, which means that when we receive God’s truth and promises, our lives will be renewed and restored.

So let us work every day to keep a joyful heart, and seek the good news that brings us joy and nourishment. When we face life’s challenges with a joyful heart, we will be able to meet each day with faith, hope, and love.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May your soul be filled with gladness and your life be nourished. May you keep seeking good news in your daily life and face challenges with a joyful heart. Amen!

v: Yet he didn’t leave himself without witness, in that he did good and gave you rains from the sky and fruitful seasons, filling our hearts with food and gladness.”
b: In this passage God reminds us that His grace and love are always present, and that He gives us food to the full and hearts filled with gladness. In the same way, in our lives God also gives us countless blessings and joys.

There was a boy named Ruixiang, an orphan who had lived in an orphanage since he was small. He had no parents’ love and no family warmth. But he had a heart full of joy. Every day he worked hard at his studies and greeted everyone with a smile. His joy touched the other orphans, and also the staff and volunteers at the orphanage.

One day a philanthropist came to the orphanage. He was moved by Ruixiang’s joy and decided to adopt Ruixiang as his own son. From that day, Ruixiang had a family of his own, with the love and care of parents. His life changed from then on. He was no longer lonely, but full of joy.

This story tells us that even in difficulty and lack, we can have hearts filled with gladness. The grace God gives us is so abundant, and His love and compassion will never run short. Like Ruixiang, let us bring joy to every corner of our lives and let our joy be a blessing to others.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you be filled with gladness every day and feel God’s grace and love. “Amen!”

v: Now may the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace in believing, that you may abound in hope in the power of the Holy Spirit.
b: In life we often face all kinds of challenges and difficulties, and these may make us lose faith and hope. Yet this passage reminds us that we have a God of hope, and through faith He fills our hearts with all joy and peace.

Imagine a dark night in which we walk along a rough path full of thorns, our hearts filled with fear and unease. We have lost our way and do not know where to go. But suddenly we see a ray of light shining from far away, and as the light grows stronger, our spirits grow brighter. That light is God’s love and blessing, and through faith He kindles in our hearts the flame of hope and joy.

This hope and joy are not based on how good or bad our surroundings are, but on our faith in God. It is like a person guarding a candle in the wind and rain. Even though it is utterly dark all around, as long as the candle keeps burning in his hand, he has light in his heart and knows that one day the dawn of peace and joy will come.

In our lives there may be many hard times that leave us discouraged and in despair. But when we turn to faith, to God, He fills our hearts with all joy and peace. This is God’s promise, and He wants us to abound in hope through the power of the Holy Spirit!

So whatever trouble you face now, do not give up hope and joy. Believe God’s word; He will fill your heart with all joy and peace. Like that bright ray of light, your life will become bright through faith, and you will be full of faith, hope, and love.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you: May you find hope in difficulty, see light in darkness, and find fulfillment in longing. May God’s joy and peace fill your heart, and may your life be full of faith, hope, and love. Amen!

v: Therefore, my brothers, beloved and longed for, my joy and crown, stand firm in the Lord in this way, my beloved.
b: In this passage, Paul writes to the church in Philippi, full of love and gratitude for the brothers and sisters there. He calls them his joy and crown, what a beautiful description! Here Paul urges them to stand firm in the Lord, which means to rely steadfastly on God through trials and difficulties.

Each of us has faced hardship and challenges, and sometimes we feel weak and disheartened. But when we turn our eyes to God, we find that He is our strength and firm foundation. Just as Paul encouraged the brothers and sisters to stand firm in the Lord, when we place our faith in God, He gives us strength and courage to face every difficulty.

A young man named Rongjie had an exceptional gift for basketball, but in high school he suffered a serious leg injury and needed a long recovery. The injury nearly cost him his hope and dream of basketball. Yet he did not give up. Every day he stayed faithful to his therapy and rehabilitation exercises, and he built a deep relationship with God. In the end he stood up again, returned to basketball training, and became an outstanding player.
This story tells us that even when we face difficulties and setbacks, if we trust firmly in God, He will help us overcome every difficulty and achieve our dreams.

Dear brothers and sisters, everyone meets different challenges in life, but however great the adversity, let us remember that God is our strength and firm foundation. As Paul said to the church in Philippi, you are my joy, and we too should stand firm in the Lord. Let us place our faith in God and believe He will lead us through every challenge.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you all. When you face difficulties, may God give you strength and courage, so that you can trust Him without wavering and live with joy and hope. Amen!

v: For you are our glory and our joy.
b: This passage reminds us that we who are Christians can bring one another joy and glory.

In life we often meet all kinds of difficulties and challenges that leave us discouraged and powerless. Yet in this passage God reminds us that we are not alone. When we share fellowship with other Christians and support one another, we become one another’s glory and joy. It is as though we were one big family, caring for and supporting each other.

In a small village there was an old man who dried his crops in the sunshine every day. Whenever the villagers saw how hard he was working, they gathered around him and helped him finish. Although each person had his own work to do, they supported one another and made the old man feel happy and honored. The old man no longer felt lonely, because he knew he was loved and cherished.

In the same way, we who are Christians can care for and support one another like those villagers. When we see others in need of help, we can reach out actively and give them joy and honor. This not only brings them hope and encouragement, but also fills our lives with meaning and purpose.

So let us ask ourselves every day: “How can I be someone’s joy and glory today?” or “Do I need to ask others for help and support?” In this way, as we help one another, we can experience God’s blessing and guidance.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you find true joy and glory as you care for and support one another. Amen!

v: Every man also to whom God has given riches and wealth, and has given him power to eat of it, and to take his portion, and to rejoice in his labor—this is the gift of God.
b: In this passage we see that God’s purpose in giving us wealth is not only to supply our needs, but even more to let us find joy in our labor. It is like a farmer who works hard every day, plowing the land and watering the crops, looking forward to the harvest season. When he sees the crops grow and bear fruit, he is filled with delight and gratitude. In the same way God gives us resources and wealth, so that we can eat and enjoy and receive our rightful portion. This is not only a material blessing, but an expression of God’s love and grace toward us.

In this world we also go through all kinds of toil and hard work. Sometimes we may feel weary, disappointed, or anxious, but it is precisely in these difficulties that we can find God’s joy. Think of a businessman who works hard, overcomes all kinds of challenges, and finally achieves success for his company. He is not only pursuing wealth and position; he also enjoys the sense of accomplishment and delight that his hard work brings.

The joy God gives us in our labor also reminds us of the value and meaning of life. Do not focus only on results, but cherish every step of the process. Think of an artist who meets all kinds of setbacks and difficulties in the process of creating. Yet it is these very challenges and refinements that make his work more vivid and interesting and show his talent and creativity.

So whatever difficulties we meet at work, in our studies, or in daily life, let us remember that God gives us joy in our labor. Do not focus only on reaching the goal; enjoy the whole process with a thankful heart. Although we may face setbacks and failures, let us believe in God’s grace and guidance and walk with Him.
So let us look for joy in our labor, keep faith in difficulty, and treat ourselves and others with love. May you feel God’s grace and joy in every moment of your hard work.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you experience God’s rich blessing in your life every day. Amen!

v: I know that there is nothing better for them than to rejoice, and to do good as long as they live.
b: This passage reminds us that in this world there is one thing more important than anything else: to rejoice and do good all our lives. Throughout our lives, no matter how great the challenges and difficulties we meet, we can face them with joy and by doing good.

Imagine a very clear morning, the sun pouring down warm light and filling the whole world with vitality. Our lives can be as bright and happy as this morning. When we have a joyful heart, we can not only feel God’s lovingkindness, but also bring this joy to the people around us.

Doing good is a very important element in our lives. By doing good we can help others and give them hope and love. Think of a kind person who, on a cold winter day, sees a homeless person and gives him his own coat, letting him feel warmth and care. Such a good deed not only changes the homeless person’s life, but also brings inner joy and happiness to the kind person.

And rejoicing and doing good all our lives is closely tied to our faith. We believe that God is the source of love, and that He gives His love to us, so we should also pass this love on. When we face difficulty and pressure with a joyful heart, we will find that God’s peace and strength stay with us throughout our lives.

So let us face everything in life with a joyful heart each day. Even when we meet challenges and difficulties, let us persist in doing good and spread love and hope. Let us be like the sun, giving off warm light, so that the world is filled with joy and love.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you feel God’s love and grace on the path of rejoicing and doing good all your life. May you face the challenges and difficulties of life each day with a joyful heart. Amen!

v: “Whereas you have been forsaken and hated, so that no one passed through you, I will make you an eternal excellency, a joy of many generations.
b: This passage tells us that even if we have been forsaken and hated, feeling lonely and ignored, God is able to change our lives, make us an eternal excellency, and turn our lives into a joy of many generations.

In our lives we may sometimes also feel cast aside or overlooked, whether at work, in the family, or in social relationships, and we may meet setbacks and difficulties. But we should not be discouraged by this, because God’s word reminds us that He is able to change our situation.

We can imagine a desolate desert with no green and no life. Our lives may likewise have seasons full of drought and despair. Yet even in that wasteland, with just a tiny bit of water, a small seed can begin to sprout.

In the same way, God can give us hope and change in our hardest moments. His grace is like a spring that can moisten our withered souls. We only need to be willing to open our hearts to Him and believe His promises and plans, and He can give us new life in our wilderness.

The Bible records that Moses led the Israelites out of the slavery of Pharaoh in Egypt. They crossed a wilderness and faced hunger and thirst. But when they longed for water, God performed a miracle for them, opening the rock and letting water gush out for them to drink. This was God’s promise and leading for them. He not only supplied what they needed to live, but also gave them the refreshing of life.

So when we face difficulty and dryness, let us turn our eyes to God and believe He can give us joy and hope in our wilderness. As this passage says, even if we have been forsaken and hated, God can make us an eternal excellency and bring us a joy of many generations.

So let us believe firmly that whatever difficulty we are in now, God can change our situation. He is a faithful, loving, and almighty God, and He will not abandon us. When we face challenges, let us seek His help and guidance, and believe His promises and plans.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you all. May you believe God’s promises on your life’s journey and experience His joy and hope. May your life become a joy of many generations, and in every difficulty may you see God at work. Amen.

v: The LORD, your God, is among you, a mighty one who will save. He will rejoice over you with joy. He will calm you in his love. He will rejoice over you with singing.
b: This passage tells us that our God is a God who loves us. He is not only the Lord who saves us, but also the guide in our lives. When we meet setbacks and difficulties in life, He is at our side, giving us strength and comfort. He loves us quietly, and He rejoices over us with singing because of our joy.

There was a man named Ruide who had always felt inferior and discouraged. He felt he was worthless and that no one cared about him. He was always sunk in melancholy and could not find a source of happiness.
One day Ruide walked into a church and heard a sermon on this passage. A power rose up in his heart, and he began to believe in God’s love. He decided to give himself to God and follow His guidance.

From that day, Ruide’s life began to change. He learned to let go of his inferiority and discouragement and accept his own worth. He began to feel God’s presence in his life and found joy in the midst of difficulty.

Like Ruide, when we give ourselves to God and believe in His love and power, we too can feel from within the source of joy. Whether it is challenges at work, problems in the family, or personal worries, God is with us, giving us strength, and rejoicing over us with singing because of our joy.
Let us look every day for signs of God’s love and praise Him in joy. When we face the many difficulties of life with a joyful heart, we will find how deeply God’s love and power touch our lives.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you feel God’s love and joy every day. Amen!

v: Until now, you have asked nothing in my name. Ask, and you will receive, that your joy may be made full.
b: In this passage Jesus tells His disciples an important truth: when we ask in the name of Jesus, our joy will be made full. This is an encouraging message. It reminds us that our God is loving and powerful, and that He is willing to hear and answer our prayers.

In our lives we often meet difficulties and challenges that leave us discouraged and disappointed. Sometimes we may feel we cannot bear any more pressure and hardship. In these moments, Jesus’ words remind us that when we bring our needs and difficulties before God, He will hear and answer our prayers.

There was a young boy named Jiade who came from a poor family. His parents were often worried about making a living, and the family’s financial pressure also affected his mood. In this hard time, Jiade began to seek God’s help and guidance.

Every evening he would find a quiet place and pray earnestly to God. He told God about his family’s difficulties and needs, and entrusted his life to God’s plan and leading. Although the difficulties were still there, Jiade’s heart was full of hope and joy, because he knew his God heard and cared about his prayers.

As time passed, God began to do wonderful things in the lives of Jiade and his family. Little by little they saw God’s provision and blessing. Their finances improved, and family relationships became more harmonious. Jiade knew it was all God’s grace, and his joy and gratitude overflowed all the more.

This story tells us that when we bring our needs and difficulties before God, He hears and answers our prayers. As long as we ask in the name of Jesus, our joy will be made full. For God’s love is boundless, and He is willing to show His great power in our lives.

So let us ask in the name of Jesus every day and bring our needs and difficulties before God. Believe His promise, knowing He will answer our prayers and make our joy full. Even if difficulties and challenges continue, we can have faith and hope, knowing that God’s love and blessing will be revealed in our lives.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you ask in the name of Jesus every day and bring your needs and difficulties before God. May your joy be made full, and may you keep growing in God’s love and blessing. Amen!

v: make my joy full by being like-minded, having the same love, being of one accord, of one mind;
b: In this passage Paul writes to the believers of the church in Philippi, reminding them to love one another and to pursue God’s will with one mind and purpose. And what is the result of this? It makes Paul’s joy full.

In life we may face all kinds of outside pressure and difficulty that leave us discouraged and robbed of joy. But when we live out love and a common mind as Christians, not only do we ourselves benefit, but we also bring hope and joy to those around us.

We can imagine a family in which parents and children are always of the same mind and the same love, with one heart and one purpose. They respect and care for one another and work together toward the family’s goals and happiness. Such a family environment is sure to be full of joy and warmth.

In the same way, in the church, when every believer pursues God’s will with the same mind and purpose, we become a harmonious community, supporting one another and reaching common goals. This spirit of unity not only makes our faith stronger, but lets us experience in life the joy and peace God gives.

Take a small group whose members serve together in the church, of one mind, one love, one heart and one purpose. Whatever difficulties come, they can always face them united. For example, when the church holds a large event that needs everyone’s cooperation and effort, if each person does his part and serves with love and a spirit of offering, the task can be completed smoothly. Such teamwork brings spiritual joy to one another and lets more people come into contact with God’s love and peace.

So let us face the challenges of life with the same mind, the same love, and one heart and purpose. Whether in the family, in the church, or in the workplace, let us hold to this principle and influence and change our surroundings with the love of Christ.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. I hope that as you get along with others and pursue God’s will, you may have a true joy that is your own. May you fulfill the mission God has given you with love and righteousness, and may God’s joy fill your heart in the process. Amen!

v: In the same way, you also should be glad and rejoice with me.
b: In this passage we receive a very important and beautiful guide: to rejoice together with others. Joy is a very special emotion; it can fill our hearts with strength and blessing, and it can also be contagious to others.

Let us imagine a scene: a cold winter day, snowflakes falling on the ground, and an elderly grandmother walking alone down the street. She looks a little tired and lonely, but suddenly a group of young people pass by, happily throwing snowballs at each other and laughing as they play. The old woman is caught up in their laughter and can’t help joining their game, her face shining with a happy smile. This scene tells us that joy is not only our own; it can be shared with others.

In life we often meet all kinds of people and situations. Sometimes we may face challenges, pressure, or difficulties, and then we need to support and encourage one another. As the apostle Paul wrote in Philippians, “In the same way, you also should be glad and rejoice with me.” He kept a joyful attitude in hard circumstances and encouraged others to do the same.

Let us learn to rejoice with others, whether in times of success or of failure. When we share joy with others, we not only deepen our relationships but also build bonds of faith, hope, and love among us. Through laughter, embraces, and encouragement we can let everyone feel God’s lovingkindness and blessing.

Today, whatever situation you are in, let us rejoice together. Let us face every challenge with joy and thanksgiving and share this joy with others. When we support and encourage one another, we will find that joy can bring more blessings and miracles.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you rejoice with others at all times, and find faith, hope, and love in your joy. Amen!

v: In this you greatly rejoice, though now for a little while, if need be, you have been grieved in various trials,
b: This passage tells us that as Christians we should have joy. But this does not mean we will always be in joy, because in life we all meet all kinds of trials and difficulties. These trials may be health problems, challenges at work, trouble in relationships, or even the loss of a loved one.

When we face trials and difficulties, we may feel sorrowful, helpless, or even in despair. Yet let us remember that this sorrow is only for a little while. Just as the dawn must come after the night, the difficulties and sadness we go through will also pass.

It is like a seed buried in the soil under heavy earth. It is a long and hard process. Yet it is in exactly such an environment that the seed can take root, sprout, and grow strong. Our lives are the same: trials and difficulties can become opportunities for us to grow and become strong.

There was a man named Jianming who lost his parents when he was young and lived in great hardship. But he was not discouraged. He kept studying hard and found meaning in life amid hardship. In the end he became a successful businessman and philanthropist. He went through many trials, but he always kept a joyful attitude.
In the same way, when we feel sorrow in trials, let us seize the opportunity to learn to trust God and look for joy in difficulty. For God promises that those who are faithful will have great joy.

So whatever difficulty you are going through, remember it is temporary. Believe God’s word and keep seeking joy and hope in hardship. Just as that seed can finally grow strong, you too can grow and triumph in trials.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you keep joy, hope, and love in difficulty. May you see God’s grace and guidance in every trial. Amen!

v: whom, not having known, you love. In him, though now you don’t see him, yet believing, you rejoice greatly with joy that is unspeakable and full of glory,
b: In this verse we are reminded that even though we have never seen the Lord Jesus with our own eyes, we can love Him through faith. This faith fills our hearts with inexpressible joy and glory.

There is a story about a young man. In his life he met countless setbacks and difficulties that drove him to despair. But when he began to learn to trust the Lord Jesus and grow in faith, he found a joy rising in his heart that he could not express. This joy was not based on outward circumstances, but came from his faith in and love for the Lord Jesus. Though he still faced difficulties, his heart was filled with true joy.

This story reminds us that when we love the Lord Jesus in faith, we experience a true joy. This joy is not limited by outward circumstances but is built on our relationship with the Lord Jesus. Even when we are in hardship and adversity, through faith we can experience this inexpressible joy.

At the same time, this verse reminds us that our faith and love are visible evidence. When we walk through the world full of faith, hope, and love, our lives become a glorious testimony that displays God’s power and glory. Our lives will become an attraction, letting people see our relationship with the Lord Jesus and feel that inexpressible joy.

So let us live out this great joy full of glory every day, whatever our circumstances or difficulties. Let us love the Lord Jesus in faith, and let this joy become the most beautiful testimony of our lives.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you experience inexpressible joy in faith; may your life become a glorious testimony that displays God’s power and love; and may you live out this great joy full of glory every day. Amen!

v: For I rejoiced greatly when brothers came and testified about your truth, even as you walk in truth.
b: In this passage we see an important truth: people’s conduct and the truth they believe are inseparable. When we are in adversity, when our faith is being tested, whether our conduct matches the truth we proclaim is a question every Christian needs to consider.

There was a young man named Joseph who came from a poor family but had a heart full of hope and faith. He believed in God’s promises, and he believed in his own abilities and effort. He worked hard at his studies and his job, and offered what he had learned and earned to God.

One day Joseph met with a difficulty: his coworkers tried to tempt him onto a crooked path. It was an opportunity to test his faith. But Joseph held fast to his faith and refused the temptation, because he knew it did not agree with the truth he held in his heart.

Joseph’s conduct became a testimony. His coworkers saw his perseverance and integrity, and they were moved by his faith. One day a coworker came to Joseph and told him that he also wanted to believe in God, and hoped to learn how to walk in the way of truth.

This story tells us that our conduct and the truth we believe are connected. When we walk according to the truth, our conduct becomes a testimony that can move and inspire others. Like Joseph, each of us can be an instrument of God, bringing love, hope, and faith to those around us.

So let us work every day to walk in the truth, whatever our circumstances, holding fast to our faith and becoming witnesses to the truth. May our conduct inspire and encourage others and bring them faith, hope, and love.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you receive spiritual growth and blessing as you walk in the way of truth. Amen!

v: “All nations shall call you blessed, for you will be a delightful land,” says the LORD of Armies.
b: This passage tells us that when God blesses us, the place where we live also becomes a land of joy. God’s grace and blessing affect not only our own lives, but are passed on to the people around us and to the whole community.

Imagine that when we experience God’s rich blessing in our lives, the joy within us is like a ray of light that lights up the place where we are. When we live out faith, hope, and love, that place begins to give off an atmosphere of joy.

It is like a garden: as long as it receives enough sunshine and water, the flowers will bloom in beautiful colors and give off a lovely fragrance. In the same way, when we grow strong in God’s grace and blessing, we can show those around us a life full of love and joy.

This passage also reminds us that God’s blessing touches not only our personal joy but also whole nations and the world. When we care for others in faith and love and share God’s love and truth, we can be God’s representatives and bring joy to all nations and peoples.
Let us ask ourselves: has the place where we live already become a land of joy? Are we spreading God’s joy in our lives, giving others hope and love?
dc:
In the name of the Lord, I bless you. In every season of life, may you experience God’s abundant blessing and bring this joy to the place where you live. May you be a radiant witness, living out God’s calling in faith, hope, and love.
Amen!

t: Blessed Are Those Whose God Is the Lord
v: Blessed is the nation whose God is the LORD, the people whom he has chosen for his own inheritance.
b: In this passage God tells us that those whose God is the Lord are blessed. If we make God our God and let Him guide our lives, we will experience the blessing God gives. This blessing is not only material abundance, but even more the spiritual joy, peace, and contentment.

When we choose the Lord as our God, we become God’s inheritance, and He chooses us as His people. What glory and grace this is! As God’s people, we will receive God’s care. He will look after our needs, protect our lives, and lead us on the right path.

This passage reminds us that our blessing is not only for our own enjoyment but is to be shared with others. Just as God chose us to be His people, we too must care for those around us, help them come to know God, and bring them the message of the gospel. When we become a blessing in others’ lives, we too will feel great joy and fulfillment.

This passage helps us understand that it is a blessing to trust God and take Him as our God. Let us put God at the center of our lives every day, seek His will, and let His love and grace fill our lives. When we walk with God, we will experience spiritual abundance and the blessing God gives.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you take the Lord as your God in all things and receive the blessing He gives. May you be a blessing in the lives of others, and may God’s love and grace be made known in your life. Amen.

t: Blessed to Have the Lord as God
v: Happy are the people who are in such a situation. Happy are the people whose God is the LORD.
b: In this verse we can see what true blessing is. Being blessed does not lie in how much wealth we have or how much material abundance we enjoy, but in coming upon such a situation, having God as our God, and only then can we truly feel blessed.

Sometimes in life we may get lost in the difficulties of reality. We may experience setbacks, failures, and pain that leave us discouraged and disappointed with life. Yet this verse reminds us that as long as we have God as our God, we are blessed.

We can imagine a person who has all wealth and splendor yet lacks peace and joy within. And we can also imagine a person who has not a penny and lives in poverty, yet has God’s presence, and whose heart is full of peace and joy.

Today, whatever your situation, I want to tell you that if you come upon such a situation, that is, if the Lord is your God, you are blessed. God’s presence and love are shown in our lives and bring us faith, hope, and love.

When you face difficulty, remember this truth. Do not let setbacks and failures wear down your faith. Believe that God’s grace and power can lead you through hardship. Believe God’s promises and know that He is always with you, wherever you are, in whatever circumstances.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you remember this truth whenever you face any challenge, and receive strength and hope from it. Amen.

t: Blessed to Dwell in God’s Courts
v: Blessed is the one whom you choose and cause to come near, that he may live in your courts. We will be filled with the goodness of your house, your holy temple.
b: This passage reminds us how blessed it is to dwell in God’s house! When we draw near to God and live in His courts, we experience wonderful blessing. God’s dwelling place refers not only to a church or a place of worship, but also to our souls, our inner world.

Just as a person living in a beautiful palace enjoys the comfort and splendor it brings, when we live in God’s dwelling place we also feel God’s goodness. This goodness goes beyond the world. It is not material enjoyment, but comes from God’s grace and blessing.

Imagine a person living in a place surrounded by love, who feels safe and valued. In the same way, when we live in God’s courts, we know that we are chosen and loved by God. This love makes us feel blessed, because we know we are not alone and that there is a God who is always with us.

Besides this, living in God’s dwelling place also lets us draw closer to Him. Our communion and connection with God become more frequent, we can hear God’s voice more clearly, and we understand His heart. Such closeness brings us hope and faith, because we know that as long as we are with God, we will receive His guidance and help.

Let us think about how to live in God’s dwelling place in our daily lives. It may mean spending time each day reading the Bible and praying, seeking God’s face, and entrusting ourselves fully to Him. It can also be done by joining worship gatherings and having fellowship with other Christians.
Let us walk with God with joyful hearts every day, live in His dwelling place, and experience the goodness God gives. May God’s name be glorified in your life,
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you! May your faith, hope, and love keep growing. Amen.

t: Blessed to Dwell in God’s House
v: Blessed are those who dwell in your house. They are always praising you. Selah.
b: In this passage God reminds us how blessed it is to dwell in God’s house, and dwelling in God’s house means not only being in a church, but a life joined to God’s presence and walking with God.

Imagine what it would be like if we lived in God’s house. First, we would surely feel God’s love and peace. Just as in a church we can find calm and comfort, in God’s house we can enjoy God’s love, and His presence will fill our hearts.

Second, living in God’s house means we experience a closer relationship with God. When we focus on being before God and communicate with Him in prayer, our spirits are joined with God’s Holy Spirit. Such an intimate relationship lets us understand God’s will and plans more deeply.

Yet living in God’s house is not only for our own benefit, but for praising Him. Psalm 84:4 tells us that those who dwell in God’s house are always praising God. This reminds us that when we feel God’s grace and lovingkindness, we should respond to Him with thankful hearts and words of praise.

Let us bring this truth into our lives. Wherever we are, at home, at work, or in the community, we can see ourselves as God’s house. By following God’s will and showing God’s love and justice, we can be God’s house and bring faith, hope, and love to others.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you feel God’s love and peace as you dwell in God’s house; may you have a closer relationship with God and understand His will more deeply; and may you respond to God with a thankful heart and words of praise. Amen.

v: Blessed are those whose strength is in you, who have set their hearts on a pilgrimage.
b: In this verse we see a wonderful promise that God gives to those who rely on Him and long to go to Zion. Zion represents the glorious dwelling place of God, a place of spiritual growth and goodness. In every part of our lives we can apply this promise to ourselves.

When we rely on God’s strength, we find that we have greater power in faith, hope, and love. Just as a hiker needs strong legs to climb a high mountain, we need to rely on God to have the spiritual strength to face the challenges and difficulties of life.

Longing for the highway to Zion also means that we desire to grow and advance in our spiritual life. This road may be full of hardship and testing, but as long as we hold on to faith and hope, God’s love and strength will lead us forward.

One day a mountain climber decided to climb a high mountain. He had heard there was a beautiful lake at the summit, so he began his climb full of anticipation. Along the way he met many steep trails and sharp slopes, but he did not give up, because he knew the lake at the top was worth all the effort and difficulty.

At last the climber reached the summit, and he was amazed by the scene before him. The lake was clear to the bottom, the shores were studded with flowers, and mountain birds flew through the air. He felt how worthwhile his effort had been, and his spirit was set free and restored.

This story tells us that when we are willing to make the effort to pursue spiritual growth, we will experience visions and wonders. Just as the climber reached the summit, we too can experience the abundance of faith, hope, and love in God’s love and strength.

So let us rely on God’s strength every day and long to grow in our spiritual life. However great the difficulties we face, as long as we hold fast to faith and hope, God will surely lead us across every mountain and onto the highway to Zion.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you keep receiving strength and lifting on the road of seeking God’s will. Amen.

v: Happy is he who has the God of Jacob for his help, whose hope is in the LORD, his God,
b: On life’s journey we often face difficulties and challenges. Sometimes we feel discouraged and helpless, not knowing how to face these problems. But Psalm 146 tells us that when we look to Yahweh our God, we are blessed.

Imagine a mountain climber who, on his way up a high mountain, comes to a steep and rugged stretch. He feels his strength failing and is exhausted in body and mind. Yet he does not give up. He looks up toward the summit and believes he is able to reach it. This story tells us that when we look to God, like that climber, we can overcome difficulties and win the victory.

Looking to God is an attitude, a state of mind. When we look to God, we believe in His power and kindness and trust His guidance. We no longer rely on our own cleverness or strength, but entrust everything to God. This faith and hope let us rise above hardship and experience God’s wonderful works.

When we face challenges at work, we can look to God and believe He will give us wisdom and strength to overcome the difficulties. When we suffer illness or exhaustion in the body, we can look to God and believe He will heal us and give us strength. Whatever difficulty we face, as long as we look to God and believe in His great power, we can experience His blessing and help.

So let us take the God of Jacob as our help every day and look to Yahweh our God. Whether on a hard journey or in a joyful moment, let us trust His guidance and provision. When we look to God, we will experience His endless lovingkindness and grace, and enjoy true blessing.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you experience His blessing and help as you look to God. May you find strength in difficulty and feel God’s presence in joy. Amen.

t: Blessed to Take Refuge in God
v: Oh taste and see that the LORD is good. Blessed is the man who takes refuge in him.
b: This passage reminds us that in life, when we take refuge in God and rely on Him, we can taste the sweetness and abundance of the Lord’s grace. Just as after taking a bite of delicious food we can feel its flavor and satisfaction, when we take refuge in God we can truly experience His goodness.

But what does it mean to take refuge in God? Taking refuge in God does not refer merely to a superficial faith, but to relying on God completely and seeking His wisdom and guidance in all circumstances. In a storm, if we shelter under a sturdy tree, we are protected. In the same way, when we take refuge in God’s arms, we receive His protection and help.

Perhaps you are facing difficulties and challenges, feeling lost and helpless. Do not be afraid. As long as you take refuge in God’s arms, He will surely give His grace and strength. Just as a father who sees his child in trouble rushes to help at once, God will help us in the same way.

Blessed is the one who takes refuge in God! When we trust God completely, He will take care of all our needs and give us peace and joy. Just as flowers bloom in beautiful colors in the sunshine, when we take refuge in God, our lives too will bloom with abundance and beauty in His grace.

So let us taste the Lord’s grace every day and feel His goodness. Whatever difficulties we face, as long as we take refuge in God’s arms, we can experience His blessing and grace. Let us take refuge in God every day, rely on His grace and strength, and live a life full of faith, hope, and love.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you experience God’s goodness and grace on your journey of taking refuge in Him. Amen.

v: Blessed is the man who makes the LORD his trust, and doesn’t respect the proud, nor such as turn away to lies.
b: In life we often face all kinds of challenges and difficulties. Sometimes we may fall into arrogance or be led astray by false things. But this verse tells us that those who rely firmly on God are blessed.

Think of young David, who trusted God with all his heart. When he faced the giant Goliath, he was not troubled by outward arrogance and prejudice, but believed in God’s power and promises. So he successfully defeated the giant, became a brave warrior, and in the end became king of Israel.

This story reminds us that when we face difficulties and challenges, we should trust in God. Whether it is pressure in society, difficulty at work, or problems in relationships, as long as we trust God with all our hearts, He will surely lead us to victory and blessing.

In our lives we sometimes also meet false things that tempt us to turn away from the right path. It may be the pursuit of wealth and fame, or the pursuit of fleshly pleasures. But this verse reminds us to stay alert and not be deceived by these false things. Like David, let us hold fast to our faith in God and believe His truth.

When we persist in trusting God in our lives and are not affected by arrogance and falsehood, we are blessed. This does not mean we will not face challenges, but through faith, hope, and love we can meet these challenges, and under God’s keeping and guidance come out of our troubles and receive true happiness.
dc:
In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you trust firmly in God in your life, not be troubled by arrogance and falsehood, and experience His blessing and guidance. Amen!
In life, trusting in Yahweh is one of the important lessons for us Christians. Trusting in Yahweh means that we completely trust His guidance, believe that He will take care of our needs, and entrust our difficulties and worries to Him.
First, building an intimate relationship is the key to trusting in Yahweh. This can be done through prayer, reading the Bible, and communion with God. When we spend time connecting with God, we can understand His heart better and learn how to entrust everything to Him.
Second, learn to let go of control. We often hope we can control everything, but in fact we cannot fully control the future. Trusting in Yahweh means letting go of control and believing He will make the best arrangements for us. This may sometimes require us to set aside our own plans and wishes and submit to God’s will.
In addition, handing our burdens to God is another key to trusting in Yahweh. When we face difficulties and troubles, we often tend to solve the problems ourselves, but this only brings more anxiety and pressure. Instead, we should learn to hand our burdens to God, believing that He has the power and wisdom to solve the difficulties we face.
Finally, thanksgiving is one of the key elements of trusting in Yahweh. Whatever environment or situation we are in, we should learn to give thanks. Thanksgiving can change our view of things and help us see more of God’s goodness and the work He is doing in our lives. Thanksgiving can fill our hearts with joy and peace and strengthen our faith in God.
In summary, trusting in Yahweh requires us to build an intimate relationship, let go of control, hand our burdens to God, and keep giving thanks. These practical and effective ways can help us trust God more deeply each day and experience His boundless lovingkindness and grace. Let us learn every day to trust in Yahweh, and believe that He will lead us out of difficulty and bless our lives.

v: LORD of Armies, blessed is the man who trusts in you.
b: In this passage God reminds us that those who trust in Him are blessed. So what is trusting? Trusting is like a small child jumping into a parent’s arms and feeling safe and protected. When we trust in God, we put down our pride and self-confidence and depend completely on God’s strength and wisdom.

In life we often meet setbacks, difficulties, and pain. Some people try to solve problems with their own abilities, but find themselves sinking deeper and deeper, their strength failing. Yet when we learn to trust in God and entrust everything to Him, we find that He is our help and our firm rock.
Let us hear a story about how one person learned to trust God when she met a great difficulty.

There was a young woman named Keli. Keli met a huge challenge at work, and she felt utterly helpless and in despair. She tried every method but could never solve the problem. In the end she decided to put down her pride and began to trust in God.

Every day Keli spent time in prayer, entrusting her difficulties and worries to God. She also sought wisdom in the Bible and found verses that could guide her forward. Through faith and hope, Keli began to see God at work in her life.

God opened her eyes and let her see a way to solve the problem. He gave her wisdom and courage and helped her find a strategy for resolving the difficulty. During this time Keli learned to depend completely on God, and she witnessed God’s faithfulness to her.

Friends, when we learn to trust in God, we will find that He is our true help and hope. Whatever challenges we face, God will be at our side, giving us strength and wisdom. He is the rock we trust in, and in Him we can find peace and joy.

In this passage we see that those who trust in God are blessed. So let us put down our pride and learn to depend completely on God’s strength and wisdom. When we trust in God, we will find that He is our true help and hope. Let us seek God’s will every day and entrust everything to Him.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you receive strength and wisdom as you learn to trust in God, and see God at work in difficulty. May your faith, hope, and love keep growing as you walk with God. Amen.

v: “Blessed is the man who trusts in the LORD, and whose confidence is in the LORD.
b: In this verse God calls us to learn to trust in Him. Trusting in God is not casually saying “I believe in God,” but an attitude of deep dependence on and trust in God. Such people are blessed, because they can receive true comfort and protection from God.

A small boat was drifting on the sea when a storm suddenly struck, and the boat was in great danger. Everyone on board was in a panic and did not know what to do. But there was a brave captain who trusted in his own experience and skill. He stood at the bow, raised the helm, and relied wholeheartedly on his own ability. Yet the storm kept battering fiercely, and the boat in the waves could capsize at any moment.

But another captain had a different attitude. He believed he was limited, and that only by trusting in the Lord of the sea could he and those on board be protected. He held on to God’s word and was convinced that God was their refuge and strength. When the storm came, this captain did not stand with his chest out, but knelt in prayer and entrusted all the outcomes to God.

What was the result? Because the first captain relied on himself, the boat finally capsized, and those on board suffered heavy casualties. But because the second captain trusted in God, although the storm came, God protected them with His hand and brought them to a safe place.

This parable tells us an important truth: when we learn to trust in God, we can find firm comfort and strength in the storms of life. The world is full of uncertainty and difficulty, but when we rely wholeheartedly on God, He will surely keep us and lead us to a way out into the light.

So let us be like the second captain every day and learn to trust in God. However great the challenge we face and however fierce the storm, let us trust God’s promises and believe in His grace and power, for only in Him can we truly find comfort and protection.
dc:
In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you depend deeply on God every day and entrust all of yourself to Him. May you experience God’s grace and great power on life’s journey, and find faith, hope, and love in difficulty. Amen
390 Soul Snack. Dear Lord, I come before You, thanking You for Your matchless grace and lovingkindness. In this difficult time, I know that only by trusting in You can my strength be restored and renewed.
Lord, as the Bible says, You are our refuge and shelter, our help and provider. In this world full of challenges and uncertainty, I hold faith and hope and rely on Your grace and promises.
Give me wisdom and guidance, that in my choices and decisions I may submit to Your will. Help me understand that Your plan is better than my plan, and Your ways are higher than my ways. Let me trust Your leading completely, not relying on my own wisdom but looking to Your truth and guidance.
Lord, when I feel weak and powerless, add to my strength. When I feel fear spreading, give me a peaceful heart. Let me remember Your word: “These things I have spoken to you, that in me you may have peace. In the world you have trouble; but cheer up! I have overcome the world.” (John 16:33)
Protect and watch over me and my family, and let us find refuge under Your wings. Make our faith firm, trusting in Your promises, so that whatever the difficulty, we may face it with joyful and thankful hearts.
I believe You are a God full of kindness and faithfulness, and that Your eyes are always watching over Your people. Show Your great power and wonders in our lives, so that the world may see our testimony and know that You are our God, the source in whom we trust.
Lord, I cry out to You; hear my prayer. May Your name be honored and glorified forever. Amen.

v: Blessed are those who keep his statutes, who seek him with their whole heart.
b: In our lives we all pursue happiness and blessing. We want to have success, wealth, and joy, but God’s word tells us that true blessing comes from keeping God’s statutes and seeking Him with the whole heart.

A man was lost in a dense forest and did not know how to get out. He felt despair and confusion, not knowing what to do. Then one day he found a map that marked the route to the exit. He began to study the map carefully and move forward according to its directions. Although he met difficulties and obstacles now and then, he kept going until at last he successfully walked out of the forest.

This story tells us that when we keep God’s statutes and seek Him with our whole heart, we are like that man lost in the forest who has found the way out of life.
